title: Vinted vs Facebook Marketplace: Which Is Better for Buying & Selling Second-Hand? (UK)
intro: Vinted and Facebook Marketplace are both free ways to buy and sell second-hand in the UK, but they work very differently — Vinted is a protected, fashion-focused marketplace, while Facebook Marketplace is an open local classifieds board with almost no buyer protection. This guide breaks down the real differences so you can pick the right one.

body.heading: The short answer: different tools for different jobs
paragraphs: Vinted and Facebook Marketplace are both free to use, but that's where the similarity ends. Vinted is a dedicated second-hand marketplace built around fashion, with integrated shipping and a Buyer Protection system that holds payment until delivery. Facebook Marketplace is a local classifieds board bolted onto Facebook — no built-in payment escrow, no structured categories for clothes, and far weaker protection.
The practical rule: use Vinted for clothes and anything you'd post, use Facebook Marketplace for bulky items, furniture, and local cash sales where you can meet the buyer face to face.
This guide walks through fees, protection, audience, shipping, and what actually sells on each, so you can pick per item rather than committing to one platform.

body.heading: Fees: both free, but one has a buyer fee
paragraphs: Vinted charges sellers nothing — no listing fee, no commission, no final value fee. The buyer pays a Buyer Protection fee of roughly 5% + £0.70 at checkout, on top of the item price and shipping. The seller receives the full price they set.

Facebook Marketplace charges nothing at all — no seller fee and no buyer fee. If you sell locally for cash, the entire transaction is free. If you use Facebook's shipping option (where available), Facebook may add a selling fee on some categories, but local cash sales cost nothing.
So on pure cost, Facebook Marketplace is marginally cheaper for the buyer, but the difference is small and the protection you get for Vinted's 5% is worth far more than the fee — read on.

body.heading: Buyer protection: Vinted wins by a mile
paragraphs: This is the biggest difference. Vinted holds the buyer's payment and releases it to the seller only after the item arrives and is confirmed — and if it never arrives, arrives damaged, or isn't as described, the buyer opens a claim and gets refunded. Read [how Vinted Buyer Protection works](/guides/vinted-buyer-protection) for the details.

Facebook Marketplace has essentially no buyer protection for local sales. You hand over cash and take the item — if it's broken, fake, or not as described, you're relying on the seller's goodwill, and Facebook won't refund you. For Marketplace shipping, Facebook offers some purchase protection, but it's patchier and less established than Vinted's.

The implication for buyers: for anything over pocket-money value, Vinted is dramatically safer. Facebook Marketplace's 'collection only' sales are the highest-risk way to buy second-hand, because there's no escrow, no refund route, and no platform intervention if it goes wrong.

body.heading: Shipping vs local pickup
paragraphs: Vinted is built around integrated shipping. You choose a package size when listing, and when it sells Vinted generates the label. Integrated shipping means lost or delayed parcels are handled through the courier with Vinted's support — protecting both buyer and seller.

Facebook Marketplace is built around local pickup. The default is meeting in person and exchanging cash, which is great for furniture, large items and things that don't post well — but it also means no courier protection, no tracking, and the need to coordinate a meeting.
If you want to buy something specific from anywhere in the country, Vinted wins. If you want to shift a sofa to someone two streets away without posting it, Facebook Marketplace wins.

body.heading: Audience and what actually sells
paragraphs: Vinted's audience is people shopping for second-hand fashion — clothes, footwear, accessories, and home — who search by brand and browse catalogues. It's the better platform for clothing, especially branded pieces, because the search and category system matches buyers to what they're looking for.

Facebook Marketplace's audience is local and general. People browse it for furniture, electronics, cars, baby gear, and bulky household items. It's weaker for clothing because there's no structured size/brand system, and listings get lost in a feed of everything from sofas to cars.

The honest take: for clothes, Vinted is the clear winner. For furniture, appliances, and large household items sold locally, Facebook Marketplace is the natural fit. Many people sensibly use both — Vinted for the wardrobe clear-out, Marketplace for the garage clear-out.

body.heading: Safety when meeting Facebook Marketplace buyers
paragraphs: Because Facebook Marketplace lacks Vinted's escrow, the safety burden falls on you. If you do meet in person: meet in a public place during daylight, never give out your home address until you have to, and never hand over an item before the money is in your hand or your bank account.

Watch for the classic Marketplace scams: fake payment confirmations, overpayment followed by a 'refund the difference' request, and buyers who insist on paying by bank transfer in advance and then never show. Cash on collection, or a bank transfer you can see land in your own app, is the safe route.

By contrast, on Vinted you should keep everything in the app — any buyer or seller who asks to move off-platform is a red flag, and [Vinted scams](/guides/vinted-scams-buyer-protection) are largely avoided by staying inside the payment system.

body.heading: Which should you choose?
paragraphs: Choose Vinted for clothes, shoes, accessories, and anything you'd post — you get buyer protection, integrated shipping, a fashion-focused audience, and a structured search system. Choose Facebook Marketplace for bulky items, furniture, appliances and local cash sales where meeting in person makes sense.

The two aren't really competitors so much as complementary tools. A serious seller lists clothes on Vinted and heavy items on Marketplace, using each platform for what it's best at. For the full comparison landscape, see [all the Vinted alternatives](/guides/vinted-alternatives) and [Vinted vs eBay](/guides/vinted-vs-ebay).

Whichever you use for selling, the fundamentals are the same — good photos, honest descriptions, and realistic pricing. Start with our [complete guide to selling on Vinted](/guides/how-to-sell-on-vinted) and apply the same discipline on Marketplace.

faq.question: Is Vinted or Facebook Marketplace better for selling clothes?
faq.answer: Vinted, clearly. It has a fashion-focused audience, a structured brand/size search system, integrated shipping, and Buyer Protection. Facebook Marketplace is better for bulky items, furniture and local cash sales — it's weaker for clothes because listings get lost in a feed of unrelated items.

faq.question: Does Facebook Marketplace have buyer protection?
faq.answer: Not for local collection sales — you hand over cash and take the item, with no refund route if it's broken or fake. Facebook offers some protection for shipped orders, but it's patchier than Vinted's Buyer Protection, which holds payment until delivery and refunds you if something goes wrong.

faq.question: Are Vinted and Facebook Marketplace both free?
faq.answer: Yes for sellers — both are free to list and sell. On Vinted the buyer pays a ~5% + £0.70 Buyer Protection fee; on Facebook Marketplace local cash sales are completely free, though Facebook may add a selling fee on some shipped orders.

faq.question: Is Facebook Marketplace safe?
faq.answer: It can be, if you meet in a public place during daylight and only hand over items once payment is confirmed. It lacks Vinted's escrow and refund system, so the safety burden is on you. Watch for fake-payment and overpayment scams, and never pay by irreversible transfer in advance.

faq.question: Can I sell the same item on Vinted and Facebook Marketplace?
faq.answer: Yes, and for different item types it makes sense — clothes on Vinted, bulky items on Marketplace. Just keep your inventory in sync and remove an item from the other platform the moment it sells, so you don't sell the same thing twice.
